claims.text: The event is a 30-second window from patient SLEEP_SC401, recording sleep_SC4012E0, starting at 1989-03-31T07:27:30+00:00 and ending at 1989-03-31T07:28:00+00:00.
The detector predicted the window as an anomaly with reconstruction error 77.78 and anomaly margin 69.66, exceeding the threshold of 8.12.
The model is a shared multivariate reconstruction model (model_id 8) trained on patient SC400 and validated on SC402.
The overall anomaly threshold is the 99th percentile of validation-normal stable stage 2 reconstruction errors.
EEG Fpz-Cz channel had a residual threshold flag with normalized margin 1.84.
EOG horizontal channel had a residual threshold flag with normalized margin 9.61 and contribution share 0.968.
EEG Pz-Oz channel did not have a residual threshold flag, with normalized margin -0.29.
Attention evidence is window-level temporal relevance with no channel owner; peak relevance at 07:27:44.9, mean 0.0033.
The previous night recording sleep_SC4011E0 had 139 anomalies out of 1103 windows, an anomaly rate of 12.6%.
Representative previous-night anomalies occurred during recorded wake stages, with reconstruction errors up to 55.40.
The official Sleep-EDF hypnogram annotation for this window is stage W (wake).
Auxiliary signals show respiratory oro-nasal values ranging 187-339, submental EMG around 4.97e-06, and rectal temperature around 37.01°C.
The current event's reconstruction error (77.78) is higher than any previous-night representative anomaly error (max 55.40).
